I have heard that the Way of the Buddha is vast and boundless, its radiance illuminating all things; it existed prior to heaven and earth and is without beginning.
Arising after heaven and earth yet having no end, its essence takes purity as its primary principle and universal salvation as its function.

Its power of aspiration is vast and profound, delivering and uplifting immeasurable beings. It extends to the furthest reaches of billions of kalpas past and the furthest reaches of billions of kalpas future;
for it maintains a single thought of compassion and an impartial bestowal of grace. Thus, from the Western Land...

Hatred. They revolve in cycles of resentment and greed, racing after the fleeting pleasures of the moment, until they rapidly fall into the sufferings of the three miserable realms.
It was for these beings that the World-Honored Buddha extended his compassion; he opened the gate of skillful means and established the rite of repentance for all.

As his imperial journey now dwells above, my grief and longing are boundless;

therefore, I venture to fulfill my Imperial Father’s sacred will by ordering artisans to carve and publish this scripture so that it may be widely distributed. This is intended to enable all people throughout the world and for generations to come...
Throughout the world, even those who have reached the limits of existence all know how to return their sincerity to the Buddha-way.
Those with transgressions seek to reform themselves for a new beginning; those who love goodness exert themselves further to advance.

The blessings of my late Emperor Father and Empress Mother in the realm of Heaven shall be inexhaustible. I respectfully preface this at the beginning of the scroll.

The Buddha taught that the gate of mindfulness of the Buddha (buddhānusmṛti) is opened through the single method of visualization. This is for the purpose of bringing pure mindfulness to full maturity.

By recollecting the Buddha, the spirit dwells in the Land of Peaceful Nurturing (Sukhāvatī), where one attains a clear vision of its adornments—both the primary and secondary—so vivid they appear before the eyes.

Thus, those who practice visualization are aided by the recitation of the name, and those who recite the name are supported by visualization; in this way, the Dharma-gate of the Pure Land perfectly returns to the true mark (bhūtalakṣaṇa).

For a beginner, pure mindfulness is difficult to maintain consistently. However, if one becomes thoroughly familiar with the environment and inhabitants of the Pure Land (the *shōjō* and *ishō*), then mindfulness will manifest as soon as it is brought to mind;

thus, it is not difficult to ensure that pure mindfulness continues uninterrupted. Regarding the sutra, there are commentaries and sub-commentaries that make it easy for readers to understand, yet the exegeses by Tiantai and Siming are the most exquisite and profound.
These works enable one to know how to employ the three contemplations of emptiness, provisional existence, and the middle within a single mind to achieve perfect illumination.
It elucidates the three truths within the ultimate and conventional, and profoundly realizes the three virtues of dharma-body, prajñā, and liberation in the land of tranquil light (sukhāvatī).
Alas! How magnificent is this printed edition! It has been unheard of in distant or near regions, and its circulation has been extremely limited.
In the autumn of the year Wuyou, I met with Mr. Wang Yuan-an and Mr. Bei Jianxiang, who praised it and urged its republication. I therefore encouraged [the project].

The assembly’s efforts culminated in its completion within half a year; this is truly a cause and condition of great merit and virtue. One should know that this work stands alongside the *Commentary on the Amitābha Sūtra*:
one elucidates the practice of reciting the name, while the other elucidates the visualization of the Buddha. Together, they bring the perfection of pure karma to its ultimate height.
They must not be neglected! They must not be neglected!
